# Compress Consecutive Ranges

## Problem

## Requirements

- You receive a numeric array whose elements are already arranged in sequence.
- Traverse it from left to right, combining neighboring values whenever each next value is exactly 1 greater than the previous one.
- For any combined sequence containing two or more numbers, output it as `first to last`.
- A sequence containing just one number must be output as that number alone.
- Write every resulting compressed range on a separate line.

## Examples

Input:

```
[4,5,9,10,11,14,20]
```

Output:

```
4 to 5
9 to 11
14
20
```

The values 4 and 5 form one consecutive range, as do 9, 10, and 11; 14 and 20 have no adjacent successor in the input, so each is printed by itself.

## Notes

- Do not rearrange the array before processing it. Sorting changes the intended behavior, since results must reflect the given ordering.
- Only groups with at least two elements qualify for range formatting (`length >= 2`).

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Traverse the sorted array while tracking a current range, extend it as long as the next element is exactly the previous plus one.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

When a break is detected, output the current range—either as a single number or as 'first to last'—then start a new range.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Watch for edge cases like an empty array or a sequence with no consecutive pairs (all singletons).

</details>
